findings.claim: Flashcard [8]: "What affordable 1980s device put multitrack recording in the home?" - answer "The Portastudio - an affordable cassette-based multitrack recorder." The L3 key fact also lists the Portastudio among "five major technological developments" of the 1980s.
findings.truth: The first Tascam Portastudio (model 144) was launched on 22 September 1979, not in the 1980s. It did spread through home studios during the 1980s, and spec 3.2.2 places the Portastudio in the 1980s technology list, so the lesson's decade mapping is the examinable one. No edit: correcting the decade would put the lesson at odds with the spec a learner is assessed against.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia 'Portastudio' (Tascam 144, 22 Sep 1979, 4-track compact cassette, $899); spec 3.2.2 lines 2370-2377

findings.claim: Practice [1] mark scheme ("Identify two musical elements that define the disco style") credits "synthesised bass lines (1)".
findings.truth: Classic disco bass was normally an electric bass guitar (Chic, the Bee Gees); synthesised bass is the Moroder/'I Feel Love' exception rather than a defining element. The lesson body never teaches synth bass for disco, so no learner can produce that answer from the content. The credit is generous, not mark-costing, so it is left alone.
findings.evidence: L3 content_html disco paragraph (four-on-the-floor kick, lush strings, ~120 BPM); spec 3.2.1 / 3.2.2

findings.claim: The bottom mark band is labelled "Lower band (1-2)" in all six banded mark schemes (the 6-mark and 8-mark questions in L1, L2 and L3). In the 8-mark schemes it sits directly under "Lower-mid band (3-4)".
findings.truth: House band vocabulary is Top band / Upper-mid band / Mid band / Lower-mid band / Low band, so the bottom band should read "Low band". "Lower band" next to "Lower-mid band" also reads ambiguously. Not a banned string and not a factual error, so no edit is made here; a one-word label sweep would fix all six at once if Tom wants the labels consistent.
findings.evidence: house band vocabulary in the checker brief; L1 practice [4] and [5], L2 practice [4] and [5], L3 practice [4] and [5]
